intro: Once learners can count, they learn to compare: which group has more, which number is bigger, and how to put numbers in order. This is the start of seeing numbers as having sizes and places.

I.2.01.what: Telling which of two groups has more or fewer by pairing the items up one to one.

levels.a: Pairs up two small rows and spots which one has some left over.
levels.b: Pairs up two rows to decide which has more.
levels.c: Pairs up two rows to decide which has fewer.
levels.d: Says how many more one row has, by counting the leftovers.

I.2.02.what: Recognizing when two groups have the same number of things, even if they look different.

levels.a: Checks whether two rows have the same number by giving each item a partner.
levels.b: Works out how many to add to make two groups the same.
levels.c: Finds groups with the same number even when arranged differently.
levels.d: Counts to check, instead of assuming a longer row has more.

I.2.03.what: Using a number line from 0 to 10, where numbers sit in order along a line like steps.

levels.a: Works out which number belongs at a marked spot on the line.
levels.b: Finds where a given number sits on the line.
levels.c: Makes jumps of 1 forward or back along the line.
levels.d: Fills in several missing numbers on the line.

I.2.04.what: Deciding which of two numbers up to 10 is bigger or smaller.

levels.a: Picks the bigger number, with pictures to help.
levels.b: Picks the smaller number, with pictures to help.
levels.c: Uses the number line: the number further right is bigger.
levels.d: Compares two numbers with no pictures or line to help.

I.2.05.what: Using a number line from 0 to 20, including the teen numbers.

levels.a: Places teen numbers, like 12, on the line.
levels.b: Counts how many numbers lie between two numbers.
levels.c: Finds the number a few steps before or after a given number.
levels.d: Makes jumps forward and back along the line and says where they land.
levels.e: Finds the number exactly halfway between two numbers on the line.
levels.f: Works out how many equal jumps of 2 it takes to get from one number to another.

I.2.06.what: Putting a set of numbers in order from smallest to biggest, or biggest to smallest.

levels.c: Picks out the greatest and the least in a small list.
levels.d: Orders numbers up to 100, in either direction.

I.2.07.what: Using position words like first, second and third to say where something is in a line.

levels.a: Uses first, second and third to name places in a line.
levels.b: Uses position words all the way up to tenth.
levels.c: Works out how many are in front of or behind someone in a line.
levels.e: Works out how many people are in front of someone, given their place in line.
levels.f: Solves a puzzle: someone is seventh from the front and seventh from the back; how many in line?

I.2.08.what: Comparing numbers up to 20 by thinking about tens and ones, or using a number line.

levels.a: Compares teen numbers by looking at the ones, since both have one ten.
levels.b: Uses a number line to decide which number is smaller or bigger.
levels.c: Decides whether statements like "7 is more than 15" are true or false.
levels.d: Solves short stories asking who has more or fewer.

I.2.09.what: Comparing numbers up to 100 by looking at the tens first, then the ones.

levels.a: Compares two-digit numbers by their tens, such as 78 and 87.
levels.b: Compares numbers with the same tens by looking at the ones.
levels.c: Decides which ten a number is closer to, such as 88 being nearer 90.
levels.d: Solves short stories comparing numbers up to 100.

I.2.10.what: Using the signs = (the same as), > (greater than) and < (less than) to compare numbers.

levels.b: Chooses > or < between two small numbers; the open side faces the bigger one.
levels.c: Writes comparisons with these signs for numbers up to 20.
levels.d: The same with numbers up to 100.

I.2.11.what: Making a sensible guess of how many there are without counting, then checking.

levels.a: Glances at a group and says whether it is more or less than 10.
levels.b: Picks a sensible estimate, like about 5 or about 20.
levels.c: Counts to check someone's guess and sees how close it was.
levels.d: Uses a group of 10 as a guide to improve a poor guess.

I.2.12.what: Working out the difference between two amounts: how many more one has, or how many fewer.

levels.a: Lines up two cube trains up to 10 and counts the extra cubes.
levels.b: The same with up to 20 cubes.
levels.c: Counts the jumps between two numbers on a number line.
levels.d: Solves short stories like "Mia has 11, Zoe has 3; how many fewer?"
levels.e: Works backwards: knows one child has 2 more and how many they have, finds the other's amount.
levels.f: Solves a puzzle: after one child gives 5 to even things up, finds how big the gap was.
